issues.where: site/targeting_content.json:599 (D-4: calls 'cite Friday's published numbers'), :618 (D-3 to D-1: 'Rescue messages now rest on Friday's published numbers'), :1221 (Rescue timing: calls through Mon 26 Oct 'citing Friday's published numbers'); route #playbook
issues.problem: The playbook tells teams to run rescue messaging that quotes poll results throughout the statutory poll-publication ban (Sat 24 – Tue 27 Oct). Repeating survey results in mass call scripts and in digital or media rescue messages during the ban is very likely a prohibited publication of a survey under Israeli election-propaganda law. At best it is untested and needs a counsel ruling. The same page's legal box says 'publish, post or leak no poll … from Sat 24 Oct', so the advice contradicts itself.
issues.fix: In :599, replace 'and cite Friday's published numbers' with 'and use threshold arithmetic only (a list under 3.25% elects no one), quoting no poll figures'. In :618, replace 'Rescue messages now rest on Friday's published numbers.' with 'From now on, rescue messages and call scripts quote no poll figures; use threshold arithmetic only.' In :1221, replace ', citing Friday's published numbers' with ', using threshold arithmetic and no poll figures'. Add to the guardrails at :1302: 'Quoting or re-publishing any poll result in campaign material, ads or scripted calls during the ban needs a written ruling from election counsel.'
issues.verifier_note: Confirmed. content json:599 says calls 'start on Saturday night after Shabbat and cite Friday's published numbers'. :618 says 'Rescue messages now rest on Friday's published numbers' during Sat 24–Mon 26 Oct, and :1221 says calls run through Mon 26 Oct 'citing Friday's published numbers'. The same site's legal guardrails (:1302) say 'From Sat 24 Oct to the close of polls, publish, post or leak no poll', and :1060 lists 'publishing polls during the blackout' as a legal grey zone. Scripted mass calls and digital messages that quote poll figures during the ban are, at the least, a publication-ban risk that needs a counsel ruling. The playbook instead instructs it.

issues.where: src/targeting_model.py:148,969,982 (list_pers = 0.003/0.22 per contact) and 1153; site/targeting_app.js:1103 ('persuasion of identified soft Netanyahu-bloc voters'), :1095 ('switches about 0.3% of them'), :1130; playbook intro ('about 3 switchers per 1,000 conversations')
issues.problem: Phone, text or relational persuasion calls are scored at 1.36% switching per contact. That is the per-cross-pressured-voter rate, 4.5x the 0.3% per soft voter the site describes. The model also assumes the campaign can identify 30% of cross-pressured soft Netanyahu-bloc voters, about 2% of the electorate, which has no source. Persuasion calls are the highest-value units in the planner, so they are allocated first.
issues.fix: State it in s.7 and the parameter table: 'List persuasion calls assume the campaign can identify cross-pressured soft voters (about 2% of voters); each completed call is scored at 0.3%/0.22 ≈ 1.4% switching.' Better, score list_pers with RHO_PERSUADE*CROSS_PRESSURE (0.3%) on n_pers/CROSS_PRESSURE targets, or apply a phone discount (×0.67). Add both variants to targeting_sensitivity.py.
issues.verifier_note: Confirmed. RHO_PERSUADE = 0.003/0.22 = 1.36% is applied per list contact (list_pers, targeting_model.py:982). The list target is n_pers = pool × p × pers_share, i.e. only cross-pressured soft voters. Mean per-contact planner value in non-Arab localities: persuasion calls 22.71 per 1k, door 2.37, supporter calls 4.58. All 7,727 persuasion-call contacts are used in every 30% plan, worth about 175 net votes (14.5% of 1,207). The site describes these as 'persuasion of identified soft Netanyahu-bloc voters' with '0.3% switch' (app.js:1095, 1103, 1130). It never states the 1.36% per-call rate or the assumption that lists hold only the cross-pressured 22%. Phone and text persuasion are also scored at door strength.
